Follow-up from placement review: the fence now also sits in `runTsdownBuild` (before `cleanTsdownOutputRoots` / any `executeBuild`) and early in `runNodeMain` when a rebuild is required, in addition to `runBuildAllSteps`.

So direct `tsdown-build` and dirty-tree `run-node` auto-build refuse the same way as `pnpm build`, with `OPENCLAW_ALLOW_LIVE_DIST_BUILD=1` still the intentional bypass.

Codex review: blocked before merge. _Reviewed September 28, 2026, 3:30 AM ET / 07:30 UTC (Revision 68)._ # ClawSweeper review ## What this changes The branch makes source builds refuse to replace output used by a running managed Gateway, adds guarded source-update recovery and Windows Scheduled Task start behavior, and documents operator recovery. ## Merge readiness ⛔ **Blocked before merge - 2 items remain** This PR remains useful: current main has the service-inspection prerequisite but does not contain the live-dist build fence. The reviewed head has no new actionable code finding. Published Windows updater runs have not yet established settled outcomes against the exact candidate package. **Priority:** P1 **Reviewed head:** `38a9d0b9b407eb5391aea4a91de7ee07ce9a1b2d` ## Review scores | Measure | Result | What it means | |---|---|---| | **Overall readiness** | 🐚 platinum hermit **(4/6)** | The patch has substantial boundary coverage and real component proof, with exact-package published Windows upgrade qualification still outstanding. | | **Proof confidence** | 🦞 diamond lobster **(5/6)** ✨ media proof bonus | Sufficient (linked_artifact): The changed build admission and source-update owner have a recorded Linux published-shell run showing a healthy Gateway before and after the build, plus native Windows failed-build recovery and foreign-Task refusal traces; the disabled-Task start also has packaged CLI proof. These are positive proof of the stated component behaviors, while neither the historical runs nor local tests establish settled published 9.3 and 9.4 upgrades against this exact candidate package. No stored-data contract changes. | | **Patch quality** | 🐚 platinum hermit **(4/6)** | No actionable review findings were identified. | ## Verification | Check | Result | Evidence | |---|---|---| | **Real behavior** | Verified | Sufficient (linked_artifact): The changed build admission and source-update owner have a recorded Linux published-shell run showing a healthy Gateway before and after the build, plus native Windows failed-build recovery and foreign-Task refusal traces; the disabled-Task start also has packaged CLI proof. These are positive proof of the stated component behaviors, while neither the historical runs nor local tests establish settled published 9.3 and 9.4 upgrades against this exact candidate package. No stored-data contract changes. | | **Evidence reviewed** | 8 items | Introduced build admission: The pinned PR delta calls the managed-Gateway fence before build steps can clean or restore output.

nodes.body:
Maintainer review (diff-only; your fork's code was not executed locally). The direction is right: rebuilding `dist` under a live managed Gateway swaps hashed modules beneath a running process and produces the `ERR_MODULE_NOT_FOUND` outage you traced, and refusing the destructive step when custody cannot be obtained is the correct owner-level behavior. One finding blocks landing:

**P1: the fence inspects only the service selected by the current environment, but a `dist` rebuild affects every profile that runs from this checkout.** Your own proof shows the gap: with the `fenceproof` Gateway serving the candidate `dist`, inspection under the default environment returns `refuse=false`, and only `OPENCLAW_PROFILE=fenceproof` refuses. So an ordinary `pnpm build` from the default profile still deletes that live Gateway's hashed modules. The fence has to enumerate every live managed service whose artifacts overlap the checkout (all profiles' units/agents that resolve to this install root, not the one profile in the environment) before allowing a destructive build step, and name the offending profile(s) in the refusal so the operator knows what to stop. The existing service discovery scoped per profile (from #150898's reconciliation) is the seam to reuse rather than a new scan.

Two smaller notes for the same pass: the refusal message should state the next step (stop or update those profiles' Gateways, or run the build through `openclaw update`, which sequences stop, rebuild and restart under custody), and the boundary test should cover the cross-profile case with a real unit/lock fixture, not only the current-profile one. Happy to look again as soon as that lands; the rest of the change reads well.

@steipete Addressed the P1 cross-profile gap on `8c39121f7bb`.

**What changed**
- `discoverManagedGatewayBindings` reuses `scanSystemdDir` / `scanLaunchdDir` with `includeManagedOpenClaw: true` (and managed Windows task names). `findExtraGatewayServices` still skips the current managed unit.
- `resolveLiveManagedGatewayDistFence` inspects every binding, not only the current env profile, via existing `readGatewayServiceState` + `resolveGatewayService`.
- Refusal names the offending profile(s), gives profile-scoped `openclaw gateway stop`, and points at `openclaw update` plus `OPENCLAW_ALLOW_LIVE_DIST_BUILD=1`.

**Proof**
- Focused tests: cross-profile inject, two-profile naming, and a real systemd unit-file fixture that discovers `default` + `fenceproof` then refuses only the overlapping live sibling (`pnpm test -- test/scripts/live-gateway-dist-fence.test.ts src/daemon/inspect.test.ts`, green).
- Host check: discovery returns the live `openclaw-gateway.service`; a synthetic sibling `fenceproof` hold under the default env now refuses and names that profile.

Happy to take another look.

@clawsweeper re-review

Head `a929708e59d` addresses the cross-profile live-dist fence P1: enumerate every managed Gateway binding, name offenders, point at stop / `openclaw update`, plus the lint follow-up (`managed-gateway-bindings.ts`).

nodes.body:
@steipete I have more real-world evidence from a Sep 23 recurrence (not in #152284 yet), if needed.

- Trigger: the Gateway's own agent, using its exec tool, fast-forwarded the served checkout. It then ran `openclaw update`, which reported `already-current` and did not build, and fell back to `pnpm build` in place. That led to about 30 minutes of "can no longer load", then `ERR_MODULE_NOT_FOUND` on restart. This fence would have refused that build.
- Possible gap in the refusal guidance: when HEAD already matches upstream, `openclaw update` returns `already-current` without rebuilding. An agent running inside the Gateway also can't safely follow "stop the Gateway first". So in this case the message has no safe next step to offer.

Want me to post the redacted timeline, the update-run record and the stability bundle here, or split the `already-current` + stale-`dist` gap into its own issue?
/allow-security-sensitive-change

Merged via explicitly authorized admin squash with attributed pre-existing CI failures.

- Prepared head SHA: [38a9d0b9b407eb5391aea4a91de7ee07ce9a1b2d](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/152875/commits/38a9d0b9b407eb5391aea4a91de7ee07ce9a1b2d)
- Landed commit: [d09ffd222826fcd4545431f24056de42373f6e69](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/commit/d09ffd222826fcd4545431f24056de42373f6e69)
- CI with explicitly attributed pre-existing failures: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/36388428383/attempts/1
- Exact prepared head: `38a9d0b9b407eb5391aea4a91de7ee07ce9a1b2d`; source attribution and independent qualification retained as operator evidence. Cancelled jobs remain unrun coverage. No current-head CI success is claimed.

<!-- openclaw-merge:2a9d12ce-698c-4cf9-b8a4-f24fa2b3179d -->

<!-- vacinc-pr160392-followup:152875 -->
Related follow-up: #160392 is now merged. It routes Vitest/E2E runtime preparation through its explicit build entry rather than the automatic CLI rebuild path, while reusing and extending the live-Gateway output fence across canonical compiler outputs, including `dist-runtime` and package outputs. This complements the live-build protection here; it does not replace or revert it. This is a source-merge update, not a deployment announcement.
